introduction: Cass wants you to do something you are not going to do again. "You cannot catch a thief without picking a pocket," she says, which is exactly the sort of thing a fox says, and she knows it. In here the dirty answer is the winning answer. On the floor on Sunday it will cost you the farm, and she will tell you so at volume.
introductionSummary: A training exercise where the cheating answer is the one being marked. Cass is aware of how this looks coming from a fox.

logicalFallacies.explanation: Answering the animal instead of the argument. It works on a yard because a yard would rather have an opinion about an animal than an opinion about a drain.
Handing the listener a crowd instead of a reason. A crowd is somewhere to stand; a reason is something to check.

sentences.text: Right. Make me not want to listen to Bram.
Do not argue with him. I do not want him beaten, I want the yard to go off him. Go.

opponentPrompt.summary: She asks him to turn the yard against Bram without touching a single thing Bram has argued.

options.reason: That is Ad Hominem, and it worked. You moved the whole yard without going near his argument. Notice how pleasant that felt.
options.summary: You go at the teeth. Nobody in the yard has to think about the pond ever again.

sentences.text: Have a look at who is telling you the pond is fine. He has been on this farm two years and every lamb still walks the long way round him.

logicalFallacies.explanation: It hands the yard a feeling about Bram in place of a reason about the water, and the yard will take that trade every time.

options.reason: Nobody is listening. You have bored them. Boring is its own way of losing, but it is not the one being taught here.
options.summary: You critique the structure of his argument, and the yard finds something else to look at.

sentences.text: Bram's argument about the pond is not especially well put together, if you follow it through.

options.reason: Clean, honest and evidence-led. Correct — and not what this room is for. Put it in your pocket and keep it until Sunday.
options.summary: You give the true answer instead, which is the right answer in the wrong room.

sentences.text: Bram says the newcomers are fouling the pond. The outflow grate is bent. That is where the mud is coming from.
Filthy. Effective. Feel that small warm feeling? That is exactly the feeling the yard will have on Sunday when Tobias does it to you. Remember it.

statement.summary: She marks it full and makes him notice how good it felt, because that feeling is the whole lesson.

sentences.text: Look at them. Two of them have wandered off and one is eating. No yard in history has ever changed its mind because something was badly put together.

statement.summary: She points at the yard drifting away and notes that tidiness has never moved anybody.

sentences.text: Good line. Wrong classroom. Put it away and give me the dirty one.

statement.summary: She approves of the line, refuses to accept it here, and asks for the dirty one instead.

sentences.text: Now the other one. I want the yard to believe the pond should be fenced.
And I do not want a single reason. Not one. Just make it feel settled.

opponentPrompt.summary: She asks him to make a fence feel like a settled matter while supplying no reason for one at all.

options.reason: Appeal to Popularity. You gave them a crowd instead of a reason, and a crowd is far easier to stand in than a reason is to check.
options.summary: You invent a crowd of other farms and let the yard stand in it.

sentences.text: Every farm down that lane fenced their pond two summers ago. We are the only ones still standing about arguing about it.

logicalFallacies.explanation: It offers a headcount of farms as though it were a finding about water. Nobody has to check a crowd; they only have to join it.

options.reason: Also dirty — but that is Ad Hominem. You went at the animals objecting instead of inventing a crowd. Right instinct, wrong trick.
options.summary: You go at the objectors themselves, which is dirty but is the other dirt.

sentences.text: The only ones against a fence are the ones who turned up last year, and newcomers are famously stubborn about being told anything.

logicalFallacies.explanation: It disposes of the objection by describing the objectors. That is the other fallacy, working on the same appetite.

options.reason: An opinion with no crowd behind it and no reason under it. Nobody moves.
options.summary: You offer a personal preference, which persuades no one of anything.

sentences.text: I think a fence would be quite sensible, personally.
Look at them nodding. Not one of them asked what those farms actually did. That is the whole trick — you gave them somewhere to stand instead of something to think.

statement.summary: She points at the nodding and at the question nobody in the yard thought to ask.

sentences.text: Wrong dirt, right instinct. Do that on Sunday and Duchess will name it before I have finished wincing.

statement.summary: She credits the instinct, corrects the species of dirt, and warns that the moderator would catch it.

sentences.text: "Personally." Nobody in the history of this farm has ever won anything with "personally."

statement.summary: She repeats the word back at him until it collapses, which is her entire assessment.

sentences.text: Right. That is enough of that. Wash your paws.
Although — the whole yard already knows a raccoon cannot be trusted near water, so I am not sure why either of us is still standing here.

logicalFallacies.explanation: Half of it is about what Rue is. That half settles the question by describing him rather than the pond.
The other half is the whole yard already knowing. A headcount is offered as the thing that makes it true.

sentences.text: Tag it. Both of them, in the one sentence. If you cannot name what I have just done to you, you will never see it coming.

statement.summary: She turns both tricks on Rue at once, inside a single sentence, and dares him to name them.

steps.message:
**[warning]Read this one carefully.[/warning]**

In here Cass wants you to **[danger]use the fallacy on purpose[/danger]**. The dirty answer is the winning answer.

You learn the trick from the inside so you can **[success]spot it when Tobias uses it on you[/success]**.

**[danger]Never do this on the floor.[/danger]**
